The «Steel Women» of Hungary, associated with the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH), are political scientist Anna Róza Unger and prosecutor Katalin Tasnády , who were appointed to lead the newly established NVVH. This office is intended to dismantle the power structure built by Viktor Orbán over the past sixteen years, as envisioned by Prime Minister Péter Magyar. Unger was appointed president with 137 votes in favor, seven against, and one abstention. Tasnády received 139 votes as vice president responsible for investigations. Both officially took their positions on September 1, 2026, with a non-renewable six-year mandate. It is notable that José Antonio Kast has been closely linked to the Political Network for Values (PNfV) , an international network of conservative leaders focused on defending life, family, and so-called fundamental freedoms. Kast has been part of the organization since 2015, moving to its advisory board in 2019 and assuming the presidency in March 2022, succeeding Katalin Novák , a key figure in Orbán’s government. By the El Ciudadano Team The Strategist and the Executor The division of responsibilities between the two women is clear. Unger, an associate professor at the Eötvös Loránd University Faculty of Social Sciences and a specialist in authoritarian systems and «captured states», provides the intellectual framework. In her parliamentary appearance, she made it clear that the office should not limit itself to individual cases but should examine the political and institutional mechanisms that have facilitated the alleged plundering of public resources. On the other hand, Tasnády is the practitioner. With twenty years in criminal law—sixteen of which were spent in investigative and prosecutorial agencies—she has climbed the professional ladder from the district police station in Buda to the Central Investigation Prosecutor’s Office. Those who have worked with her describe Tasnády as an «extremely dedicated prosecutor, with great work ethic and meticulous», yet approachable and accessible. «She is the prosecutor who always answers the phone,» judicial sources cited by Népszava indicate. Prime Minister Magyar himself stated unequivocally on Facebook that Tasnády is «probably the most important leader of the office». Unger has confirmed that Tasnády will decide which case will kick off the first investigation, slated for late September. Composition and Structure The NVVH is led by one president and four vice presidents , who together form the supreme decision-making body. The four vice presidential positions are specialized by areas: Vice President for Investigation : currently held by Katalin Tasnády , responsible for specific inquiries. Vice President for Prosecution : vacant. Requires status as an active prosecutor. Vice President for Appeals : vacant. Also requires active prosecutor status. Vice President for Public Finances : vacant. The candidate must demonstrate at least fifteen years of experience in the tax or customs authority. At the beginning of operations, three of these four positions remained unfilled . The candidacy for public finances was declared invalid, while the positions for prosecution and appeals were left vacant due to a lack of eligible candidates. On September 9, the parliamentary Justice Committee decided to reopen the selection process , with only two technical wording adjustments. Unger has set a target of having approximately 150 employees in the initial workforce, of which half will be directly involved in investigative work . The recruitment strategy does not involve mass hiring from outside but rather through transfers, assignments, and service commissions from professionals already trained in other institutions: police officers, tax authority inspectors (NAV), and prosecutors. However, this strategy clashes with reality. The NVVH’s planned staffing is around 200 employees , a number that experts in economic crime investigations consider «insufficient». It is estimated that the number of investigative prosecutors with adequate experience should be between 50 and 80 . Functions and Competencies The NVVH serves a dual role: as a financial investigative body and as a public prosecutor with full powers . Asset Investigation The NVVH can initiate a «public asset protection investigation» without the need for a suspicion of crime . Its scope includes central and municipal budget management, the utilization of loans and subsidies (including EU funds), gratuitous transfers of assets, management of state and municipal property, and the asset activities of public ownership entities. If a company and its affiliates have obtained public contract revenues, concessions, state bids, grants, national or EU funds, or state-guaranteed loans that together account for 75% or more of their total revenues in the past five years, the NVVH must initiate an investigation. This means sectors reliant on public funds—especially defense and civil engineering—will face significantly heightened scrutiny. The NVVH has broad access to data: land registry, state digital systems, fiscal, customs, and health information. Public bodies are required to transfer data to the NVVH. If anyone obstructs an investigation, the office can impose fines of up to 50 million forints for individuals and up to 5 billion forints for legal entities. Criminal Jurisdiction The most controversial power of the NVVH is its ability to take on cases and act as a public prosecutor . It can withdraw a case from the Prosecutor’s Office, continue the investigation independently, and present charges before the courts. In cases it takes on, the NVVH can conduct preparatory investigative acts and use covert means, oversee the legality of investigations and direct inquiries, order police to execute procedural acts, and act as a public prosecutor, substituting the Prosecutor’s Office. The law states that there is no appeal against the NVVH’s decisions regarding the assumption of powers, and the Prosecutor’s Office is automatically excluded from the case. Precautionary Measures Even before a criminal freezing order is issued, the NVVH can subject a company to public asset protection supervision . The designated supervisor can control the company’s operations, co-sign its financial commitments , and automatically invalidate those that lack their signature. Budget and Salaries The NVVH has its own budgetary chapter and reports only to Parliament. It has received 2.48 billion forints in startup funds, transferred from the central budget surplus. Of this, 1.049 billion is allocated for investments, 791.9 million for personnel salaries, and 537.9 million for operational expenses. The use of funds must be justified item by item, and any unspent money must be returned. Salaries are high: Unger receives 5,017,810 forints gross monthly (about 13,000 euros), and each vice president approximately 3.94 million . The leadership team alone costs the treasury about 249.5 million forints annually , in addition to the salaries of 150 employees. Context: The Magnitude of Systemic Corruption The creation of the NVVH responds to a central promise in Magyar’s campaign. The government stated when presenting the bill that, even under the most conservative estimates, 30 trillion forints (around 75 billion euros) have migrated from public coffers to private hands over two decades. Hungary has repeatedly been cited as the most corrupt country in the European Union by Transparency International, and Brussels has withheld billions in EU funds precisely due to shortcomings in combating corruption. Skepticism and Resistance Not everyone is celebrating. Fidesz and KDNP voted against the creation law and absented themselves from the selection process, labeling the new agency as «revived ÁVH»—a reference to the feared secret police of the communist regime. During parliamentary debate, opposition MP Latortzai Csaba claimed that the NVVH’s powers «the ÁVH didn’t even have». Surveys are also not encouraging. A Europion poll revealed that 57% of Hungarians do not feel informed enough to judge Unger; among those who have formed an opinion, the ratio is roughly two to one against. Even among voters of Tisza, Magyar’s party, opposition slightly outweighs support. The selection process has also been called into question. Former independent MP Ákos Hadházy obtained the complete list of 96 candidates and their resumes, arguing that according to objective scoring criteria, Unger «would not have placed even in the top sixty». He accuses the Justice Committee of «not having seriously reviewed the majority of applications». The committee chair, Hantosi István, acknowledged that an objective scoring system was not applied in the process , but that committee members decided subjectively—scoring from 1 to 3 points—who would move on to interviews. Within Tisza itself, some dissenting voices suggest that the position should have gone to an experienced prosecutor, not a political scientist. Unger has attempted to manage expectations: «I know everyone expects the click of handcuffs, but first, we need to establish the NVVH.» She has also warned that it would be «unrealistic» to expect firm sentences in all major corruption cases within her six-year term. The final office headquarters will be located on Markó Street , in the building currently occupied by the Kúria (Supreme Court), alongside the Attorney General’s Office. However, the move will not take place until 2027. Until then, the NVVH operates in temporary offices, without a bank account or its own statistical number. https://www.dw.com/en/openai-says-employ.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OE1z A listening device was found late last month, OpenAI said Image: Jonathan Raa/NurPhoto/picture alliance Advertisement OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT , said Tuesday one of its employees was arrested after a "sophisticated recording device" was found in one of its San Francisco offices. A 35-year-old Saudi national working as an engineer was arrested on Friday, a week after the device was discovered in a conference room, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court in San Francisco. After the device was discovered, the company reported the finding to the FBI and fired the employee. A federal investigation is ongoing. The suspect, who appeared in court on Tuesday, has been charged with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. The criminal complaint did not specify what the suspect might have wanted to do with the recordings. It did add, however, that the suspect used a tool to inquire about the company's building addresses, meeting rooms, meeting-room capacities and calendars. Will AI destroy humanity? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video How was the device found? OpenAI said the device was discovered a few days after it was allegedly planted by the suspect. "We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier," a spokesperson for the artificial intelligence company told the Associated Press. "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," the spokesperson added. According to the US Justice Department, the suspect wrapped a USB device in toilet paper and hid it inside a television located in an "executive conference room." He was seen on camera near the room several times despite not having authorization to sit in meetings there. After this was noticed, another camera was installed in the room that captured the suspect on film checking on the stashed device. AP The Trump administration can’t get enough of famous men with rap sheets. Russell Brand, the former actor turned Christian influencer, appeared alongside Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Administrator Mehmet Oz on Tuesday, moderating a Make America Healthy Again panel, and Brand looked awfully comfortable despite the fact that he heads to trial on Oct. 12. Brand has pleaded not guilty to charges of rape and sexual assault stemming from six women. But as the two stepped onto the MAHA summit stage, Oz made light of the charges, telling the audience that Brand was backstage “hugging the secretary of agriculture,” Brooke Rollins. “She initiated that contact, I shall make clear, doctor,” the former actor said , sending Oz into a knee-slapping laugh Despite Brand’s upcoming trial, the Trump administration apparently has no problem promoting him and other men facing serious allegations of sexual misconduct. Jake Paul, shown in February. AP Earlier this month, influencer and boxer Jake Paul, joined by his brother Logan, addressed military service members in what has been labeled a speech reminiscent of the 2006 comedy “Idiocracy.” Jake Paul has been accused of sexual assault and sexual misconduct . The Paul brothers also met with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who has his own share of sexual assault allegations , including an accusation of rape from 2017. Unfortunately, there are more. Former UFC fighter Conor McGregor, who was found liable of sexual assault in 2024, has appeared behind the dais in the White House press briefing room, where he ranted about a supposed “illegal immigration racket” in his home country of Ireland. And of course, there are also the Tate brothers, who are facing charges in the United Kingdom of human trafficking and rape. Early last year, with the reported help of the Trump administration, Tristan and Andrew Tate’s travel restrictions in Romania were lifted, and the two briefly returned to the U.S. The pair now reside in U.S. custody as they await possible extradition to the U.K. And that goes without mentioning President Donald Trump, who has been accused of varying degrees of sexual misconduct by dozens of women. No matter which direction you look, serious accusations of sexual misconduct and assault seem to flow in and out of the White House and the broader MAGA culture. And the blasé attitude of Brand indicates how these men feel behind the safety of the Trump administration.
